thread:
customer_jane: Hey team — over the last ~30 minutes our calls to /v1/generate are sporadically returning 502 and 504. Happening from eu-west-1 region. Request IDs: req_7f3a2, req_7f3a9. Our app retries once but still seeing failures. Any known issues?

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this, @customer_jane. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and the SDK version? Also which model/route are you hitting and the exact timestamps?

customer_jane: Using ruby-sdk v0.9.4 and hitting model `redwood-2-large` via our project key. Minimal curl that replicates it: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-large","input":"test","max_tokens":64}' 
  --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15
```

It fails about 1/6 requests with 502 or 504. Happened at ~2024-05-07T14:12:03Z and 14:19:47Z.

maria (support): Thanks. We're escalating. I'm opening an incident and pinging runtime/SRE. Meanwhile, can you set SDK retries to 3 and backoff to exponential? That often helps while we investigate. I'll also post ETA. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-20240507-42 — "Gateway 5xx spikes in eu-west-1". Severity: P2. Pager duty notified.

alex (eng-runtime): I'm looking at ingress and runtime traces for those req ids. Seeing NGINX upstream 502s and a pattern of partial gRPC stream resets between router and workers. Might be KV cache thrashing causing worker OOMs for a subset of long-lived sessions. Pulling logs and core dumps now.

ryan (eng-sre): I'm triaging infra. No autoscaler events, but GPU nodes in eu-west-1 did show a brief CPU steal/IO stall window right around 14:18Z. Could be a noisy neighbor spike on the host (cloud hypervisor). We're collecting dmesg and host metrics.

maria (support): @customer_jane — quick customer-facing note prepared to send if you'd like: 

"Hi Jane — we see intermittent gateway errors when routing to eu-west-1. Our engineers are investigating; we recommend enabling 3 retries with exponential backoff in the meantime. We'll follow up within 60 minutes with an update"

customer_jane: Yes please send that. Our SLAs are tight, so we need updates.

maria (support): Sent and cc'd you. (copy) :email:

alex (eng-runtime): Repro steps I used (internal): 

```python
# snippet used by eng-runtime to repro
import requests
for i in range(200):
    r = requests.post(
        'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',
        headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {TEST_KEY}'},
        json={'model':'redwood-2-large','input':'repro','max_tokens':64},
        timeout=(5,10)
    )
    print(i, r.status_code)
```

I can reproduce ~1 in 20 requests returning 502 when run from eu-west-1 test agents. Stack trace shows `worker.go` hit an encrypted-KV-cache path and then connection reset by peer.

ryan (eng-sre): Mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily shift some traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 for hosted customers with a routing policy tweak. 2) Add a short 10s upstream retry in the router for 502/504. 3) Roll hotfix to catch OOM condition and fallback to non-cached path. Rolling step 1 now.

ops-oncall: Traffic shift started. We'll monitor 10 mins and look at error rate.

support-bot: Auto-update: error-rate(eu-west-1, /v1/generate) dropped 70% after routing change. Metrics: 5xx-rate from 3.8% -> 1.1% in 8m.

customer_jane: Error rate has dropped on our side too. Still seeing occasional 504 but much fewer. Thank you.

alex (eng-runtime): Root cause summary so far (WIP): a cache path in the runtime (hot KV cache) can increase memory pressure for certain request patterns; combined with a host I/O stall on a subset of GPU nodes produced transient worker restarts and upstream 5xx responses. We've pushed a conservative hotfix to runtime to: 
- detect cache OOM and fallback to disk-backed path
- add more graceful shutdown on worker restart to avoid hard gRPC resets

We also put a short upstream retry in the router for 502/504 with jitter to smooth spikes.

maria (support): Customer comms update sent: 
"Hi Jane — engineers identified a transient memory pressure + host I/O issue in eu-west-1 causing gateway 5xxs. We mitigated by shifting traffic and deploying a runtime hotfix. You may see occasional 504s under load; we're continuing to monitor. We'll follow up with a postmortem within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption"

customer_jane: Appreciate the fast response. Can you confirm whether we should change any client-side timeouts/retries as a permanent recommendation?

alex (eng-runtime): Short answer: yes. Recommend client retries 2-3 times with exponential backoff and a request-level timeout of 20s for generate calls. We plan to update SDK docs and release a patch to the Ruby SDK to enable safe default retry logic.

ryan (eng-sre): Post-incident actions (too): 
- Add host-level noisy neighbor detection to autoscaler triggers.
- Improve router backoff for upstream resets.
- Add targeted e2e load tests for KV cache path.

maria (support): I'll include those in the incident ticket and schedule a sync with the customer for the postmortem.

ops-oncall: Confirming incident is moving to monitoring state. If error-rate remains low for 1h we'll close INC-20240507-42.

support-bot: Incident INC-20240507-42 status -> monitoring.

customer_jane: Thanks all. Please share the postmortem and any SDK changes once ready.

alex (eng-runtime): Will create a brief postmortem doc and link here when ready. Initial draft ETA 24-48h.

maria (support): Closing loop here: we've updated the customer's engineering contact and added a follow-up in 48h. Marking this thread resolved from support side for now. :white_check_mark:

customer_jane: Resolved on our side. Thanks everyone! :pray:
